claims.text: The proposed alloy is equiatomic W-V-Ta-Ti-Cr (WVTaTiCr with x=1).
The W-V-Ta-Ti-Cr coating is initially produced by laser cladding.
The initial coating contains a BCC solid-solution matrix and a network of Cr2Ta Laves precipitates.
The as-clad WVTaTiCr coating has a hardness of approximately 627 HV.
Cold rolling followed by aging will induce coherent nanoprecipitates in the BCC matrix of WVTaTiCr.
A suitable aging window is 650–900 °C for 5–20 hours.
The treatment should be followed by water quenching and conducted in an inert or vacuum atmosphere.
The treatment will create stepwise-controllable coherent precipitate interfaces.
The thermo-mechanical treatment will refine grain boundaries in WVTaTiCr.
Coherent interfaces facilitate dislocation shearing and pinning while maintaining lattice continuity.
Aging produces ordered D0a or D022 precipitates that cause order hardening and lattice-misfit strengthening.
The Cr-rich Laves phase and BCC matrix form a dense protective Cr2O3/TiO2 film during high-temperature exposure.
Coherent interfaces suppress premature cracking and thereby preserve both high hardness and ductility.
The treated alloy will have microhardness above 650 HV.
The treated alloy will retain high density.
The treated alloy will have compressive strength above 1.5 GPa.
Aging will reduce the corrosion rate in 3.5 wt% NaCl by at least one order of magnitude relative to the as-cast state.
Aging will reduce the parabolic oxidation-rate constant at 800 °C by more than 30% relative to the as-clad coating.
Temperatures above the precipitate solvus or cooling rates that are too slow will produce incoherent brittle intermetallics and reduce ductility.
The mechanism is falsified if aging produces no coherent precipitates, hardness falls below 600 HV, or corrosion exceeds 1.0 mm/a relative to the as-clad control.

contradictions.description: The mechanism attributes a dense protective oxide film to the pre-existing Cr-rich Laves phase and BCC matrix, whereas the baseline says the same as-clad phase constitution forms non-protective oxides. The hypothesis does not clearly explain how aging changes the oxide-forming role of those phases.

The predicted hardness threshold is above 650 HV, but the falsification rule only rejects hardness below 600 HV; an outcome from 600 to 650 HV would fail the prediction without falsifying the hypothesis under the stated rule.
